questions.question: A clean-contaminated wound is one in which:

options.A: A hollow viscus is entered under controlled conditions without significant spillage
options.B: A sterile elective operation is performed with no viscus entered
options.D: There is a traumatic wound more than 12 hours old

questions.explanation: Clean-contaminated: respiratory, alimentary or genitourinary tract entered under controlled conditions (e.g. elective cholecystectomy). Dirty wounds involve existing infection.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: The most reliable method of sterilising surgical instruments is:
questions.explanation: Autoclaving at 121 °C for 15 minutes (or 134 °C for 3 minutes) kills spores.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: Shock resulting from massive loss of blood volume is called:
questions.explanation: Hypovolaemic: haemorrhage, burns, dehydration. Cardiogenic: pump failure. Septic: vasodilatation due to toxins. Neurogenic: loss of vasomotor tone.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: In ATLS classification, a Class III haemorrhage involves loss of:
questions.explanation: Class I <15%, II 15–30%, III 30–40% (hypotension, tachycardia >120), IV >40%.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: Which IV fluid is used for rapid volume resuscitation in a bleeding patient?
questions.explanation: Isotonic crystalloids stay in the extracellular space; 5% dextrose redistributes into all body water and is a poor volume expander.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: Which agent is commonly used for skin preparation before surgery?
questions.explanation: Skin preparation reduces surgical site infection.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: The causative organism of tetanus is:
questions.explanation: A gram-positive anaerobic spore-bearer; tetanospasmin blocks inhibitory neurotransmitters, causing trismus and risus sardonicus.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: Gas gangrene is caused by:
questions.explanation: Characterised by crepitus, foul-smelling discharge and rapid spreading myonecrosis; treated by radical debridement and penicillin.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: The definitive treatment of a mature abscess is:
questions.explanation: ‘Where there is pus, let it out’: drainage plus antibiotics where indicated.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: Healing by primary intention occurs when:

options.A: The wound is left open to granulate
options.C: Wound edges are approximated, as in a clean surgical incision

questions.explanation: Secondary intention: wound heals by granulation and contraction; tertiary (delayed primary): closure after a few days.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: A keloid scar differs from a hypertrophic scar in that it:

options.A: Extends beyond the margins of the original wound and does not regress
options.C: Is confined to the wound and regresses

questions.explanation: Common in dark-skinned individuals; treated by intralesional steroid and pressure.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: Which vitamin is essential for collagen synthesis and wound healing?
questions.explanation: Vitamin C is a cofactor for hydroxylation of proline and lysine.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: The classical pain of acute appendicitis starts in the:

options.A: Epigastrium and radiates to the shoulder
options.C: Periumbilical region and then localises to the right iliac fossa

questions.explanation: Visceral pain from midgut, then parietal peritoneal irritation at McBurney's point.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: McBurney's point lies:

options.A: At the midpoint of the inguinal ligament
options.B: Midway between the umbilicus and symphysis pubis
options.D: One-third of the distance from the right ASIS to the umbilicus

questions.explanation: Maximal tenderness here suggests appendicitis.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: A hernia that cannot be reduced and has a compromised blood supply is:
questions.explanation: Strangulation is a surgical emergency causing gangrene of the contents.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: An indirect inguinal hernia passes:

options.B: Lateral to the inferior epigastric vessels through the deep inguinal ring
options.D: Medial to the inferior epigastric vessels

questions.explanation: Direct hernias pass through Hesselbach's triangle medial to the inferior epigastric vessels; femoral hernias lie below and lateral to the pubic tubercle.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: Femoral hernias are more common in:

options.B: Women, and have a high risk of strangulation

questions.explanation: The narrow neck of the femoral canal predisposes to strangulation.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: The classic X-ray finding in a perforated duodenal ulcer is:

options.B: Air-fluid levels in the small bowel
options.C: Free gas under the diaphragm on an erect chest film

questions.explanation: Sudden severe epigastric pain with board-like rigidity.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: The cardinal features of intestinal obstruction are:

options.C: Colicky pain, vomiting, distension and absolute constipation

questions.explanation: Adhesions and hernias are the commonest causes of small bowel obstruction.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: In acute cholecystitis, a positive Murphy's sign means:

options.A: Inspiratory arrest on palpation of the right subcostal area
options.C: Pain on release of pressure in the left iliac fossa

questions.explanation: Gallstones are the commonest cause; ultrasound confirms.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: Painless progressive jaundice with a palpable gallbladder (Courvoisier's law) suggests:

options.B: Carcinoma of the head of the pancreas
options.D: Gallstones in the common bile duct

questions.explanation: Courvoisier's law: if the gallbladder is palpable in the presence of jaundice, the cause is unlikely to be gallstones.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: In generalised peritonitis the abdominal wall typically shows:

options.A: Board-like rigidity and absent bowel sounds
options.B: Soft, distended abdomen with loud bowel sounds

questions.explanation: Rebound tenderness and guarding indicate peritoneal irritation.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: The commonest site of colorectal carcinoma is the:
questions.explanation: Left-sided tumours cause altered bowel habit; right-sided cause anaemia.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: A thyroid swelling moves upward with swallowing because it:

options.C: Is attached to the pretracheal fascia

questions.explanation: A thyroglossal cyst also moves on tongue protrusion.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: The commonest type of thyroid cancer is:
questions.explanation: It has an excellent prognosis and spreads via lymphatics.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: In a young woman a firm, smooth, mobile, painless breast lump is most likely a:
questions.explanation: Fibroadenoma is called a ‘breast mouse’ due to its mobility.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: Which sign in carcinoma of the breast indicates involvement of the suspensory ligaments of Cooper?
questions.explanation: Peau d'orange results from lymphatic obstruction.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: The Parkland formula for fluid resuscitation in burns is:

options.B: 100 mL per hour for all patients
options.C: 4 mL × body weight (kg) × %TBSA burned in the first 24 hours, half in the first 8 hours

questions.explanation: Ringer's lactate is used; monitor urine output of 0.5–1 mL/kg/h.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: The commonest type of renal calculus is:
questions.explanation: Radio-opaque; renal colic radiates from loin to groin.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: Benign prostatic hyperplasia mainly affects which zone of the prostate?
questions.explanation: Peripheral zone is the usual site of carcinoma.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: A hydrocele is:

options.A: A collection of fluid within the tunica vaginalis
options.C: A varicosity of the pampiniform plexus

questions.explanation: Hydroceles are translucent and one can get above the swelling.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: Varicose veins are caused by:

options.A: Incompetent venous valves leading to reflux and venous hypertension

questions.explanation: Great saphenous vein incompetence at the saphenofemoral junction is the commonest.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: The Trendelenburg tourniquet test assesses:
questions.explanation: Not to be confused with the Trendelenburg sign of hip abductor weakness.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: Thromboangiitis obliterans (Buerger's disease) is strongly associated with:
questions.explanation: Segmental inflammatory occlusion of medium and small arteries and veins of the limbs.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: Abdominal aortic aneurysm is usually repaired electively when the diameter exceeds:
questions.explanation: Risk of rupture rises steeply above this size.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: The most common organism causing acute haematogenous osteomyelitis in children is:
questions.explanation: Metaphysis of long bones (rich vascularity, sluggish flow) is the typical site; Salmonella is seen in sickle cell disease.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: The X-ray appearance classically described in giant cell tumour of bone is:
questions.explanation: Osteosarcoma: sunburst; Ewing's sarcoma: onion peel; fibrous dysplasia: ground glass.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: The commonest site of osteosarcoma is the:

options.C: Metaphysis around the knee (distal femur/proximal tibia)

questions.explanation: Peak incidence is in adolescents; pulmonary metastasis via blood is common.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: Ewing's sarcoma typically arises in the:

options.B: Diaphysis of long bones in children, with an onion-peel periosteal reaction

questions.explanation: Small round blue cell tumour with t(11;22).
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: Pain from an osteoid osteoma is characteristically:

options.B: Worse at night and relieved by aspirin

questions.explanation: A small nidus surrounded by sclerosis; excision or radiofrequency ablation is curative.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: Osteoporosis is characterised by:

options.A: Reduced bone mineralisation with normal mass
options.C: Reduced bone mass with normal mineralisation of the remaining bone
options.D: Soft bones due to vitamin D deficiency

questions.explanation: Osteomalacia is defective mineralisation; DEXA T-score ≤ −2.5 defines osteoporosis.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: Bilateral symmetrical pseudofractures (Looser's zones) are characteristic of:
questions.explanation: Looser's zones are radiolucent bands perpendicular to the cortex.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: In Paget's disease of bone the serum alkaline phosphatase is typically:
questions.explanation: Also bone pain, deformity (sabre tibia), deafness and risk of osteosarcoma.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: In tuberculosis of the spine, the earliest radiological sign is:

options.B: Narrowing of the disc space with erosion of adjacent vertebral margins

questions.explanation: Paradiscal type is most common; psoas abscess and kyphosis (gibbus) later.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: Perthes' disease commonly presents at the age of:
questions.explanation: Boys are affected more often than girls.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: In rickets, widening of the wrist and costochondral junctions is known as:

options.B: Rachitic rosary (beading of the ribs) and wrist widening

questions.explanation: Biochemistry: low phosphate, raised alkaline phosphatase.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: All of the following are seen in osteogenesis imperfecta EXCEPT:

options.A: Excessive bone density with increased fracture resistance

questions.explanation: Defective type I collagen; brittle bones and dentinogenesis imperfecta.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: In the Salter–Harris classification, a type II injury involves:

options.B: A fracture through the physis only
options.C: A fracture into the epiphysis only
options.D: A fracture through the physis extending into the metaphysis

questions.explanation: Type I: physis; II: physis + metaphysis (commonest); III: physis + epiphysis; IV: through all three; V: crush.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: The nerve most commonly injured in a displaced supracondylar fracture of the humerus in children is the:

options.C: Anterior interosseous nerve (branch of the median)

questions.explanation: Radial nerve is also often involved; brachial artery injury leads to Volkmann's ischaemia.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: Pulled elbow (nursemaid's elbow) is:

options.C: Subluxation of the radial head through the annular ligament in a young child

questions.explanation: Caused by sudden traction on the extended arm; reduced by supination and flexion.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: Which structure is NOT commonly associated with posterior dislocation of the elbow?
questions.explanation: Myositis ossificans traumatica (not progressiva) can complicate an elbow injury.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: The normal triangular relationship of the olecranon and the two epicondyles is lost in:
questions.explanation: In flexion the three bony points form an isosceles triangle; in a supracondylar fracture the relationship is maintained.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: A patient with a fractured neck of femur typically presents with a limb that is:
questions.explanation: Posterior hip dislocation: shortened, flexed, adducted and internally rotated.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: The most important complication of an intracapsular fracture of the femoral neck is:
questions.explanation: The retinacular vessels (from the medial circumflex femoral artery) are disrupted.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: Fat embolism syndrome typically follows fracture of:

options.A: The femoral shaft or pelvis, with respiratory distress and petechiae 24–72 hours later

questions.explanation: Classic triad: hypoxaemia, neurological changes, petechial rash.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: The nerve at risk with a fracture of the neck of the fibula is the:
questions.explanation: Results in foot drop.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: Which fracture is characterised by tenderness in the anatomical snuffbox and may be missed on early X-rays?

options.A: Fracture of the first metacarpal base (Bennett)

questions.explanation: Treat as a fracture if suspected clinically; MRI is the best investigation when X-rays are normal.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: A Bennett fracture is a:

options.B: Fracture of the neck of the fifth metacarpal
options.C: Fracture-dislocation of the base of the first metacarpal

questions.explanation: Intra-articular fracture-subluxation of the thumb CMC joint; the abductor pollicis longus displaces the shaft.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: A boxer's fracture involves the:
questions.explanation: Occurs when a clenched fist strikes an object.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: The most serious early complication of an unstable pelvic fracture is:
questions.explanation: Associated with urethral and bladder injuries.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: In fracture healing, the stage in which a soft callus forms from fibrocartilage is the:
questions.explanation: Sequence: haematoma/inflammation → soft callus → hard callus → remodelling.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: Non-union is most likely when a fracture:

options.B: Is poorly immobilised, has poor blood supply or interposed soft tissue
options.D: Is well reduced and rigidly stable

questions.explanation: Smoking, infection and NSAIDs also impair union.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: The immediate priority in an open fracture is:

options.B: Antibiotics, tetanus prophylaxis and urgent wound debridement

questions.explanation: Gustilo–Anderson classification guides management.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: The commonest joint to dislocate in the body is the:
questions.explanation: Anterior dislocation accounts for ~95%.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: A fracture of the shaft of the humerus most commonly injures the:
questions.explanation: In the spiral groove.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: Gastrocnemius recession (resection) is most commonly performed in:

options.D: Equinus deformity due to tendo-Achilles tightness

questions.explanation: Used in CTEV and cerebral palsy with equinus.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: Genu valgum (knock knee) is a deformity where:

options.A: The knees touch and the ankles are apart
options.C: The knees are apart and the ankles touch

questions.explanation: Physiological genu valgum peaks at 3–4 years; excessive intermalleolar gap needs evaluation.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: Flat foot (pes planus) in a toddler is usually:

options.C: Physiological and resolves as the arch develops

questions.explanation: The medial arch develops by 6–10 years; painful rigid flat foot suggests tarsal coalition.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: Congenital muscular torticollis is due to fibrosis of the:
